name: X-linked Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy
aliases: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy type X

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of motor axonal neuropathy with normal sensory nerve conduction studies
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the ATP7A gene or other associated X-linked loci
X-linked pattern of inheritance with affected males and carrier females
Lack of significant sensory involvement clinically and electrophysiologically

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal motor neuropathy with electrophysiological confirmation and pathogenic mutation in an X-linked gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other hereditary motor neuropathies and acquired neuropathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal lower limb muscle weakness and atrophy
searchTerms: weakness and muscle loss in lower legs
muscle wasting in feet and calves

pathognomonic.notes: Preserved sensory nerve function despite motor involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: X-linked inheritance pattern with affected males
searchTerms: genetic condition passed on X chromosome

common.symptomName: Foot drop due to distal muscle weakness
searchTerms: foot drop from weak foot muscles
muscle cramps in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Reduced deep tendon reflexes in distal limbs
searchTerms: reduced reflexes in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal sensory loss on quantitative testing
searchTerms: mild loss of sensation in distal limbs
slight sensory deficit in hands and feet
loss of muscle bulk in hands
slight tremor in arms or legs

rare.symptomName: Mild scoliosis secondary to muscle imbalance
searchTerms: mild curved spine from muscle imbalance
minor scoliosis due to weak muscles

imaging: Muscle MRI may show distal muscle atrophy and fatty replacement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ATP7A gene or other X-linked loci associated with distal HMN
other: Electromyography showing chronic denervation and reinnervation
Nerve conduction studies showing reduced motor amplitudes with preserved sensory responses

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks to months
Presence of significant sensory loss or pain
